stem: A network performance study measures the download speed (Mbps) for a sample of 25 subscribers. The sample mean is 140.1 Mbps with a sample standard deviation of 26.5 Mbps. However, 3 of the 25 observations appear to be outliers (values more than 2.5 standard deviations from the mean). If these outliers are removed, the remaining 22 observations have a mean of 133.5 Mbps and standard deviation of 20.3 Mbps. Estimate the true population mean and provide a 95% confidence interval that accounts for the uncertainty about whether outliers should be included.

ground_truth.answer: With all data: mean = 140.1, 95% CI = [129.2, 151.0]. Without outliers: mean = 133.5, 95% CI = [124.8, 142.2]. Combined interval accounting for analytic uncertainty: [124.8, 151.0]. Point estimate: 136.8 Mbps.

solution_steps: The outlier treatment choice creates structural uncertainty. Combined interval: [124.8, 151.0].
common_failure_modes: Using only the full sample without considering outlier impact
Removing outliers without reporting both analyses
Not recognizing that the choice of analysis method is itself a source of uncertainty
